## Ready next (first 15 MVP todo leaves whose milestone deps are done)

- `5.1.6` Flush peak memory (found in the 5.1–5.2 review): `SegmentWriter::finish` holds every section as a `Vec` and copies it into the output, plus the grouped postings and dense norms and keys, so a flush peaks at 2–3× `size_in_bytes`; stream sections to the output (or a `Storage` writer) and document the bound the M6 flush threshold relies on (M5)
- `5.3.11` Decoded-block caching for postings (found in 5.3): `terms()` decodes its TermInfo blocks again on each call, and each `Postings` iterator decodes, and re-verifies the CRC of, the framed blocks it reads; share decoded blocks across iterators and queries (the SPEC §10.6 block cache) and measure it in 5.5.5 (M5)
- `5.3.12` Lazy column access (found in the 5.3 review): `numeric_column` and `keyword_column` decode a whole column into 8 bytes per document; read FOR blocks on demand (SPEC §5.2.1 makes any value O(1)) so a 100M-document segment does not need 800 MB per column (M5)
- `5.3.13` Positions per document (found in the 5.3 review): `Postings::positions` decodes a block's whole positions run (capped at 2^26 values, a resource error beyond); decode only the current document's positions, on demand, so memory stays proportional to one document's term frequency (M5)
- `5.4.5` A maximum term length for `text` fields (found in the 5.5 review): `TermDict` paths are bounded for keyword fields (`MAX_KEYWORD_LEN`) and the `IdMap` (`MAX_ID_LEN`), but a text term is bounded only by the document size (the token length guard is configurable, and a registered analyzer may omit it), so a crafted text `TermDict` sharing one long suffix across all its keys passes the structural check and makes the open-time stream cost keys × path length. Decide a SPEC-wide term cap (e.g. 32 KiB, enforced by the builder and checked at open) or a walk-cost budget, then bound text `TermDict`s in `Segment::max_key_len` (M5)
- `5.4.6` Re-audit `segment/read/fst_check.rs` on every `fst` version bump (found in the 5.5 review): it re-implements fst 0.4.7's node parser to prove fst cannot panic, loop or overflow on a payload it accepts, and `fst` is pinned to `=0.4.7` for that reason; a bump compares the parser and the paths the engine uses (`get`, streams, range and automaton search) with the new code, re-runs the `fst_check` tests and fuzzes `segment` (M5)
- `9.1.0` ADR: blob upload staging and expected-id API (SPEC §18.8); update SPEC §9.3/§9.4/§9.6 (M9)
- `9.1.1` Content hasher per ADR-0002 producing `BlobId` (type from 1.10.1), chunking parameters (M9)
- `9.1.2` Streaming chunker (`Read` → chunks with CRC and running content hash) (M9)
- `9.1.3` Blob manifest (chunk list) encode/decode (M9)
- `9.2.1` Pack header/superblock + `BlobChunk`/`BlobIndex` frames (SPEC §9.3) (M9)
- `9.2.2` Append blob (dedup check by id), fsync policy (M9)
- `9.2.3` Read full / range via chunk index (mmap-backed) (M9)
- `9.2.4` Recovery: torn tail truncation, index rebuild by scan (M9)
- `9.2.5` Fuzz pack reader (M9)
- … and 11 more
